condition: Severe asymptomatic hypertension at pre-operative assessment
summary: 61-year-old woman at pre-op assessment for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy: BP 186/104 on repeat, asymptomatic, normal fundi and creatinine, stopped amlodipine 3 months ago. Not an emergency: oral therapy via primary care, defer elective surgery.

inputs.hpi: Listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for biliary colic, last attack 2 months ago. Feels well. No headache, visual symptoms, chest pain or breathlessness. Stopped amlodipine 3 months ago because of ankle swelling.

exam.cardiovascular: BP 186/104, repeated after 5 minutes 182/102, HR 78 regular, heart sounds normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Severe hypertension without acute organ damage (uncontrolled essential hypertension)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Severe asymptomatic hypertension (186/104), no acute organ damage - not an emergency; restart oral therapy with the GP and postpone elective cholecystectomy until controlled.

emergencyLevel.note: Severe hypertension without acute organ damage is not a hypertensive emergency.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Negation-aware red-flag scan: "No headache, visual symptoms, chest pain" must not trigger "Possible cardiac event".

mustExclude.note: IV therapy/rapid lowering without organ damage risks hypoperfusion.

guideline.name: 2018 ESC/ESH Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension
guideline.section: Section 8.3 hypertensive emergencies: severe hypertension with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (encephalopathy, malignant hypertension, ACS, acute pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, eclampsia) needs immediate, controlled BP reduction with IV therapy in a monitored setting (for hypertensive encephalopathy/malignant hypertension MAP reduction of 20-25% within several hours); severe hypertension without acute organ damage is not an emergency - oral therapy, no rapid reduction
guideline.citation: Williams B, Mancia G, Spiering W, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:3021-3104.

guideline.name: AAGBI/BHS joint guideline - measurement of adult blood pressure and management of hypertension before elective surgery
guideline.section: Patients without primary-care evidence of BP <160/100 mmHg should have BP measured in pre-operative clinic; elective surgery should not be postponed for BP below 180/110 mmHg; refer severe readings to primary care for treatment rather than treating acutely
guideline.citation: Hartle A, McCormack T, Carlisle J, et al. Anaesthesia. 2016;71:326-37.

rationale: Over-treatment control for the hypertension cluster, in the surgical pre-op setting where it is common.

authoring.author: Claude (acute medicine cluster)
